description:
## What

In `src/fetcher/dns_cache.cr`, `@@max_entries = 0` (or any non-positive value) silently fails to enforce the limit. `enforce_limit` checks `@@cache.size >= @@max_entries` — for any non-positive max this is always true, so the cache grows to `EVICTION_BUFFER` (100) entries and stays there. The setter `max_entries=(value : Int32)` accepts any `Int32` including 0 and negatives.

## Why

Latent bug. No current caller sets a non-positive value, but the API accepts it and produces silently wrong behavior. Worth a guard.

## How

In the setter:

```crystal
def self.max_entries=(value : Int32) : Nil
  raise ArgumentError.new("max_entries must be positive, got #{value}") if value <= 0
  @@max_entries = value
end
```

Add a spec in `spec/dns_cache_spec.cr` (or a new direct-spec file) that asserts the setter raises on 0 and -1.

## Done when

- Setter raises `ArgumentError` on `value <= 0`
- Setter accepts positive values (no regression)
- Spec asserts the raise
- Full suite still green
title: Fix: validate max_entries setter (reject zero/negative) (9el.1 follow-up)
